data.title: continuumd gates every operation, field and enum member at its IDL @since through one derived table; dated items absent below their date; RFC 0026 correction 62

data.body: [MEDIUM] The single date table does not govern every ServerReject emission path. crates/continuumd/src/daemon/capability.rs:318-324 still gates capability refusals with ProtocolVersion::new(3, 1). Negotiation refusals use since::SERVER_REJECT through handshake.rs:327,382. The conformance guard at tests/idl_conformance.rs:1729-1753 checks only handshake.rs, so it stays green if the normative date moves while capability_reject stays stale. The current equal 3.1 values mask this split. Failure modes: a capability failure can emit ServerReject below its date, or suppress it at and above a later date. Edge cases: version failures and capability failures diverge at the boundary although they emit the same dated declaration. Rollback: retain the previous fixed behavior only if the single-table claim and guard are removed. The preferred repair routes both refusal paths through since::SERVER_REJECT or one shared constructor. Monitoring: compare frame presence by refusal class for identical offered ranges. Validation: test both refusal classes immediately below and exactly at SERVER_REJECT, then scan runtime version gates and run just check.

data.reason: [MEDIUM] ServerReject capability refusals still use a hard-coded 3.1 gate outside protocol::since, and the new conformance guard checks only the negotiation-refusal path.

data.body:
[MEDIUM] The pre-3.2 field gate runs after the current-version decoder, so the daemon does not ignore every unknown optional request field. crates/continuumd/src/transport/mod.rs:793-803 decodes WorkspaceCreateRequest before dispatch. The generated decoder at crates/continuumd/src/protocol/spec.rs:650-652 therefore calls the typed optional-list decoder for file_components. Only after successful decoding does this gate erase the value. A 3.0 or 3.1 request with file_components=null, a non-list, or a malformed element gets MalformedRequest. The same request with the future field absent is served. This contradicts rule versioning.compatible_change and the stated exact field gate. The RFC itself records this residual at notes/plan/rfcs/0026-continuumd-native-protocol.md:856.

Failure modes: older-version clients get a false refusal, and a negotiated old version still exposes the newer field parser. Edge cases: JSON and CBOR null, non-list values, and malformed FileComponent members fail; absent and well-formed-but-disagreeing values take the intended old lane. Rollback: keep the residual only if the exact-gating claim is narrowed; the proper repair must make request decoding version-aware or remove fields newer than the negotiated version before typed decoding. Monitoring: count MalformedRequest for workspace.create on versions below 3.2 when the raw body contains file_components, without logging its value. Validation: in both encodings, prove malformed file_components values below 3.2 behave exactly like absence, prove 3.2 rejects those values, then run just check.

data.reason: Pre-3.2 workspace.create still decodes malformed file_components instead of ignoring the undefined optional request field.

data.body: Verified at 4c576a79: both negotiation and capability refusals now construct RejectFrame only through ServerReject::gated, which reads protocol::since::SERVER_REJECT. Boundary tests cover both refusal classes.

data.reason: Fixed at 4c576a79 by one typed ServerReject gate backed by protocol::since.

data.body: Verified at 4c576a79: transport now parses the canonical document, removes request fields undefined at the negotiated version, then performs typed decoding. JSON and CBOR tests cover malformed future values.

data.reason: Fixed at 4c576a79 by version-aware request decoding before typed field decoding.

data.body:
[HIGH] The shared predicate admits the current 3.0 surface on served 2.x connections. The IDL defines an omitted @since as 3.0 at notes/plan/schemas/continuumd-native-protocol.idl:126-132, while this function returns true for None at every ProtocolVersion. OperationSpec::defined_at feeds that result into dispatch at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/mod.rs:734-735 and recovery offers at mod.rs:1276-1279. A client negotiated at 2.x can therefore invoke every since: None operation through the current 3.x decoder, including mutation and privileged operations when its capability admits them. crates/continuumd/tests/version_gate.rs:265-298 claims every version of the major but tests only 3.0, so the served N-1 path is untested.

Failure modes: a previous-major client reaches current-major request shapes and semantics, bypassing the major-version boundary. Edge cases: 2.0 and later 2.x wrongly pass; 3.0 correctly passes; explicitly dated 3.x items correctly fail on 2.x; unknown names still fail lookup. Rollback: do not claim exact cross-version gating without a major-scoped registry. If N-1 service remains required, route 2.x through explicit 2.x definitions instead of inheriting the 3.0 baseline. Monitoring: count requests where the negotiated major differs from the registry major, grouped by operation and gate result, without recording arguments. Validation: drive every undated operation and recovery offer at 2.x and 3.0, require 2.x to use a proven 2.x registry or refuse the 3.x operation, and retain all dated-boundary tests.

data.reason: [HIGH] protocol::since::defines treats the undated 3.0 surface as defined on served 2.x connections, so current-major operations and recovery offers cross the N-1 major boundary.

data.body: [HIGH resolved] crates/continuumd/src/protocol/since.rs:97-100 now scopes every definition to the current major. Failure modes: a 2.x client cannot invoke 3.x operations or receive 3.x recovery and dated data. Edge cases: undated and dated operations, fields, enum members, malformed bodies, and handshake frames follow their specified gates. Rollback: reverting the major equality would reopen cross-major access. Monitoring: count cross-major operation requests and any result, recovery, or dated-field emission. Validation: I inspected the full persisted range and each dispatch, refusal, recovery, decode, emission, and welcome path. The range includes 2.x no-surface coverage. Tests were not run under the metadata-only reviewer scope.
